Prior-Agnostic AFDM Channel Estimation for High-Mobility LEO Satellite
Communications Using Diffusion Models
Yi Huang, Yuqing Guo
 , Ce Guo
 , Ying Wang
 , Member , IEEE, and Xufeng Guo
Abstract— Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM)
is envisaged as a promising waveform for high-mobility low
Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications. This letter proposes
a prior-agnostic AFDM channel estimation framework using
score-based diffusion models. Specifically, the score function
is learned directly on the AFDM effective channel in an
unsupervised manner, and posterior inference is performed
via likelihood-annealed Langevin dynamics using the AFDM
observation model. Upon this approach, the proposed method
avoids restrictive sparse or grid-aligned channel assumptions
and is more robust to fractional delay-Doppler off-grid
leakage. Simulations under standardized LEO channel models
demonstrate that the proposed diffusion model-based method
far outperforms conventional sparse recovery and representative
learning-based baselines, while maintaining robustness across
various parameter profiles.
Index Terms— AFDM, LEO communications, channel estima-
tion, likelihood-annealed Langevin dynamics, diffusion model.
I. I NTRODUCTION
T
HE
forthcoming sixth-generation (6G) wireless commu-
nications are envisaged to enable ubiquitous broadband
access anytime and anywhere [1], catalyze the paradigm shift
from terrestrial networks to non-terrestrial networks (NTN)
where low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites are deployed to facil-
itate wide-area coverage and flexible access for remote or
underserved regions [2]. However, the high orbital velocity
of LEO satellites induces significant Doppler shifts, leading
to time-frequency doubly selective channels under multipath
propagation [3]. Such unfavorable fading severely undermines
link reliability and induce strong inter-carrier interference (ICI)
in conventional orthogonal frequency division multiplexing
(OFDM) [4]. Therefore, novel waveforms that are suitable for
high-mobility LEO environments are urgently required.
In recent years, various novel waveforms [5] have been
proposed for high-mobility scenarios, such as orthogonal
time-frequency-space (OTFS) [3], [6] and affine frequency
division multiplexing (AFDM) [7]. Although both OTFS
and AFDM can combat severe Doppler shifts, OTFS typi-
cally incurs relatively high computational complexity due to
complicated two-dimensional (2D) inverse symplectic finite
Fourier transform (ISFFT) [3]. In comparison, AFDM maps

parameters provides strong Doppler robustness over doubly
dispersive channels while incurring lower implementation

Accurate acquisition of the DAFT-domain channel is crucial
for AFDM implementations. Classical embedded-pilot estima-
tors [9] often rely on idealized channel assumptions, while
recent research advances typically adopt grid-based sparse
recovery frameworks [10], [11], [12]. Score-based generative
models, closely related to diffusion models, have exhibited
promising potential for high-dimensional signal recovery by
learning the score function of the target distribution and
performing posterior inference via annealed Langevin dynam-
ics [13], and have recently been applied to conventional
MIMO channel estimation, while their use for AFDM channel
estimation in high-mobility LEO scenarios remains largely
unexplored.
This letter aims to develop a prior-agnostic AFDM
channel estimation framework, which does not leverage any
prior assumption on the channel. Specifically, we perform
score-based learning and inference directly on the AFDM
effective channel and incorporate the AFDM measurement
model into likelihood-annealed updates, enabling high-fidelity
estimation under practical LEO propagation environments.
Moreover, the proposed framework is not merely restricted
to the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP)-based
channel realizations. The contributions of this letter can be
summarized as follows.
(i) Unsupervised Training: We apply a score model
directly on the AFDM effective channel, and the training
is unsupervised via denoising score matching, which does
not require any explicit parametric prior, sparsity model,
or statistical channel assumptions. (ii) Adaptive Inference:
We develop an AFDM-aware inference procedure based
on annealed Langevin dynamics, which is fundamentally a
coarse-to-fine refinement that effectively balances observation
fidelity and learned structural regularization. (iii) Simulation
V alidation: Simulation results under 3GPP standardized
LEO channel models and practical noise levels validate the
superiority of the proposed framework over classical linear
estimators (e.g., LS), sparse-recovery baselines (e.g., SBL),
and representative learning-based estimators (e.g., WGAN
and L-DAMP), thereby demonstrating both precision gains
and practical applicability.

In practical propagation environments, fractional Doppler
shifts and fractional time delays can introduce significant
power leakage in the effective channel matrix of (5), thereby
weakening the sparsity of Heff. Consequently, conventional
compressive sensing (CS)-based estimators [3], [18], [19] may
incur severe performance degradation in the presence of off-
grid effects. To address this issue, we develop a diffusion
framework that directly learns the distribution of the AFDM
effective channel, enabling precise estimation of off-grid Heff.
III. S CORE -BASED GENERATIVE CHANNEL ESTIMATION
The proposed score-based generative model-driven channel
estimation scheme consists of two stages: a training stage
and an inference stage. During the training stage, we train
a diffusion model sθ by minimizing a loss function. During
the inference stage, we iteratively refine the effective AFDM
channel estimate using sθ aided by the pilot signals.

the CS approaches encounter a performance bottleneck when
SNR > 20 dB. This is because the CS approaches suffer
severely from the power leakage effect due to the off-grid

DD parameters, indicating a weak sparsity of the effective

channel but learns the channel characteristics from the training
set, the estimation performance of which is not restricted by
the power leakage effect caused by off-grid misalignment.
WGAN and L-DAMP exhibit limited model capacity and
poor generalization and their training is often unstable and
highly sensitive to hyperparameters. As a result, they typically
require retraining or extensive tuning across different operating
points, leading to low engineering practicality and deployment
efficiency. Notably, a similar performance advantage of the
score-based method is maintained even when the training set
size is reduced to 1,000 samples. With a sufficiently large
training set, the score-based channel estimation method can
approximately approach the theoretical error lower bound.
Fig. 5 illustrates the impact of the pilot length Np on
the performance of our proposed diffusion model-based
AFDM channel estimation and other methods. For a
fixed symbol number N, we change the pilot length as
{0.25N, 0.5N, N, 2N } for performance comparison, corre-
sponding to Np = 4, 8, 16 and 32, respectively. It can be
observed that when Np ≥ N, the performance of the diffu-
sion model-based channel estimation method exhibits merely
marginal improvement. When Np = 0.5N , the performance
is close to its converged level, whereas further reducing the
pilot number leads to a pronounced performance degradation.
Therefore, to balance computational complexity, estimation
accuracy, and pilot overhead, choosing the pilot number as
Np = 0.5N is the most suitable.
Fig. 4 compares the performance of the model trained
under the NTN-TDL-D profile when evaluated across all TDL
channel models. It can be observed that although the training
set only contains channel samples generated from the NTN-

TDL profiles. Compared with the other profiles, the perfor-

real-world channel measurement results into the training set
can further enhance the robustness of our proposed method.
V. C ONCLUSION AND FUTURE RESEARCH DIRECTION
This letter proposed a prior-agnostic, score-based inference
for AFDM channel estimation in LEO communications. Oper-
ating directly on the AFDM effective channel, the proposed
framework avoids restrictive channel assumptions and is robust
under practical doubly dispersive conditions. Future research
will focus on developing lower-complexity network training
and inference strategies to further improve the practical effi-
ciency of the proposed methodology. Another alternative direc-
tion is to move toward real LEO air-interface implementations,
including deployment-oriented algorithm design and validation
under realistic hardware and wireless propagation conditions.
